These frequency-run measurements capture the inverter’s dynamic response to grid frequency variations. All of the above data (voltage steps and frequency steps, at each irradiance level) were combined into our modeling dataset. For this study, we focused on using the three-phase inverter data to train the ML models. 4 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Machine Learning models and results In this section, we present the PyTorch ML models employed for inverter currents predictions. The chosen architec- tures are designed to address the challenges inherent in modeling complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent behaviors of inverters. The models under investigation include different types of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), such as LSTM and GRU, attention-based architectures (Transformers), and a convolutional neural network (CNN).
